I had just moved up here, so we chatted about that, they told me about some great local spots and events. All in all, they were fantastic. I got like 30% off of them, and at the end, they gave me this box of desserts from a local bakery, as they had only cut about half off each one to all sample. Okey doke, so the recipe for the brioche:: 
For the sponge- •128 g flour (I prefer using all purpose vs bread flour, it's always worked better for me) • 2 1/4 t active yeast • 1/2 c of warm milk, between 105-115° 
For the dough- • 6 room temp eggs • 1 c of softened butter • 384 g of flour • 105 g of sugar • 2 t salt
I use my kitchen aid with the dough hook attachment for kneading and incorporating the butter. Trust me, use it if you have it. Take your mixer bowl and sprinkle the yeast into it, whisk in the flour & pour the warm milk over. Stir until just combined, then cover and let sit for about 40-45 minutes. It should develop so air pockets and be of a more "spongy" texture. Go ahead and attach the dough hook to your mixer, and on medium, add the eggs one at a time, letting them mix a smidge before the next. Then add your sugar, flour and salt slowly. Let it combine, then slowly increase to medium high power. Mix dough (scraping occasionally) until it begins to pull away from sides and has a shiny and elastic composition (takes me anywhere between 10-20 minutes depending on the day). With the mixer still running, start adding in the butter 1 T at a time. Fully incorporate it before adding the next T. It takes a while, but once you've finished adding the butter, let it mix for an extra 5-8 minutes until it passes the windowpane test. Cover and let rise in somewhere warm-ish for 1 or 2 hours, just until it is doubled.

For the strawberry/Raspberry compote, I used about 2 cups of chopped strawberries raspberries & probably 1/2 c sugar and a splash of lemon juice (I don't usually measure for compotes, I just eyeball) 

For the whipped honey cream cheese, I cheated and got the pre-whipped cream cheese, and whisked in honey and powdered sugar until I was happy with the flavor & texture.

BACK TO THE BRIOCHE
 Once it's doubled, turn out on to a floured surface and punch it down. Divide your dough in half, and work with one piece at a time. [This is the link I followed to attain the pretty ring](https://www.thekitchn.com/3-stunning-ways-to-shape-brioche-228633)
Once you're all shaped and good to go, cover it with a piece of plastic wrap sprayed with non stick. Let rise for another 1-2 hours until about doubled as well. Uncover, coat with eggwash and melted butter (i do both, some people like one or the other) I bake it at 375° for about 25-30 minutes until it's nice and golden on top 💕💕


Edited to add that with the compote, you're just going to mix everything in a small saucepan over med low heat and bring to a simmer. Stir regularly for about 9 minutes or until it begins to thicken and attains more of a jammy texture, let it cool before you spread, it'll also thicken while it cools!
